Chasing the burn on flys is common, and it's not a bad thing. That's the pump and local fatigue from high reps and constant cable tension, and flys are a good place to feel it. Just don't treat the burn as the scorecard: what drives growth is taking sets close to failure with good control and adding reps or load over the weeks.

Keep flys as a finisher after your heavy pressing, not the main event. If you want to make them count, slow the lowering, get a full stretch at the bottom, and log the numbers so the burn comes with progress you can see.
